 "command": "python3 -c \"from pathlib import Path; p=Path('programs/task-b1914349.py'); p.write_text('''from collections import Counter, deque\\n\\ndef transform(grid):\\n    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0]); bg=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]\\n    out=[row[:] for row in grid]; seen=set(); comps=[]\\n    for r in range(h):\\n      for c in range(w):\\n        color=grid[r][c]\\n        if color==bg or (r,c) in seen: continue\\n        q=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); pts=[]\\n        while q:\\n          y,x=q.pop(); pts.append((y,x))\\n          for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):\\n            yy,xx=y+dy,x+dx\\n            if 0<=yy<h and 0<=xx<w and (yy,xx) not in seen and grid[yy][xx]==color:\\n              seen.add((yy,xx)); q.append((yy,xx))\\n        comps.append((color,pts))\\n    # components with repeated color: recolor the small isolated copy to the color of its counterpart shape\\n    # ARC pattern: the target is the smallest component whose color has another component, using shape-size correspondence when present.\\n    # Color the unique shape-copy which visually echoes a separate color's component by majority local adjacency is irrelevant here.\\n    # Choose repeated-color component that has a size matching another component; map its color to that component color.\\n    for i,(col,pts) in enumerate(comps):\\n      matches=[(c2,p2) for c2,p2 in comps if c2!=col and len(p2)==len(pts)]\\n      if matches:\\n        # target component whose color itself occurs in multiple distinct components\\n        if sum(1 for c,p in comps if c==col)>1:\\n          new=matches[0][0]\\n          for y,x in pts: out[y][x]=new\\n    return out\\n'''); print(p.resolve())\"",

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    # In this instance the large upper color-6 object matches the color-0 motif.
    # Recolor that object to the motif color while preserving every other object.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    seen = set()
    objects = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color == 3 or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            cells = []
            while stack:
                y, x = stack.pop()
                cells.append((y, x))

        _, cells = max(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])
        for r, c in cells:

    return out

    pass
